https://www.premiumtimesng.com/opinion/9.body_zh: 债务管理办公室（DMO）应逐笔公布外债存量，列明每笔融资的贷款方、日期、条款和用途，并在重组各州债务时公布涉及的州和金额。每笔贷款和债券都应以一份独立于用款机构的公开完工记录收尾。包括联邦政府在内的债券发行方，应公布每期债券将资助的项目，并持续报告项目进展直至债券到期；不应将资金拨给官方记录已注明完工的工程。根据债务管理办公室（DMO）的数据，2025年9月30日至2026年3月31日，联邦首都 territory（FCT）的国内债务从789.3亿奈拉增至3898.8亿奈拉。6个月增加约3110亿奈拉，平均每天约17亿奈拉。FCT行政当局将这一增幅归因于更多基础设施工程。然而，无论行政当局还是其他方面，都没有文件说明是谁向其放贷、贷款条款为何、获得了谁批准，以及资金用于哪些项目。FCT的案例较为极端，但并不罕见。尼日利亚的贷款通常会公开宣布、批准和签署，往往还举行仪式。但此后资金如何使用，几乎不会记录在普通公民能够找到的地方；在FCT这样的案例中，甚至连借款本身都难以看清。尼日利亚公开举债，却私下核算。对于我们大部分债务，公开记录止步于批准环节。这并非法律的本意。2007年《财政责任法》第44条第1款规定，联邦内任何希望借款的政府，都必须说明借款用途，并提交详细说明其经济和社会效益的成本收益分析。既然必须在贷款发放前说明用途，事后就应当留下记录，说明该用途是否得到实现。我们成立财政透明度与公共廉政中心（CeFTPI），正是为了建立这样的记录。其成果是“公共债务诚信”开放数据库，涵盖尼日利亚公共借款及其资金使用情况。该项目旨在加强公共债务问责，使每笔贷款都能从获批环节追踪到其建设的成果。数据库涵盖联邦政府、36个州和FCT的对外贷款及国内债券，并将每一评级与其依据的文件关联。记录缺失时，数据库会如实说明，而不会填补空白。我们将依据贷款方自身的登记册开展核查，包括世界银行和非洲开发银行（AfDB）的登记册，并参考DMO的债务报告、债券和Sukuk发行文件、州预算及审计账目，以及联邦工程部的进度记录。每笔贷款均按同一标准评级：公开记录是否显示资金确实按借款用途使用？只有独立官方记录证明项目完工，我们才认定项目已经完成。借款方对自身项目的说法并不足够。在联邦政府、36个州和FCT获得的448笔对外贷款中，凡列明美元金额者总值为987.5亿美元，但只有138笔、即31%拥有独立的完工记录。241笔、即54%的资金用途无法确定，其中168笔已经结束，金额为239亿美元。国内债务方面情况更糟。国内债券和贷款文件提及的601个项目中，只有26个有完工记录。低评级针对的是证据状况，而非任何官员的行为。被评为“证据不足”的贷款很可能得到了妥善使用，问题在于没有人能够证明。拉各斯州Shomolu综合医院直观呈现了记录缺失的状况。拉各斯州2023年5月的一份债券文件将医院翻修列为180亿奈拉项目，但支付金额为零，工程完成度为0%。2025年11月20日的第四期债券文件则将其描述为一座价值435.6亿奈拉的新医院，记录截至当日已支付12,001,840,630.57奈拉，但工程完成度仍为0%。同一份债券还为该项目额外分配了48.9亿奈拉。债务规模使这一切更加严重。2026年6月30日，公共债务总额为166.79万亿奈拉，而2016年末为17.36万亿奈拉。其中一部分增幅来自2023年对22.71万亿奈拉央行垫款（Ways and Means）的证券化，也有一部分来自奈拉贬值，但其余大部分是新增借款。如今有10个州的债务超过一整年的财政收入。卡杜纳州的债务相当于其2025年收入的336.7%，只有5个州及FCT处于财政责任委员会援引DMO数据所列50%指导线之内或以下。在联邦层面，一笔来自中国进出口银行的3.995亿美元贷款为阿布贾和拉各斯的国家公共安全通信系统提供资金。贷款已全额拨付，网络于2011年建成。2023年7月，警务部表示，该系统处于停用状态，部分设施遭破坏，必须通过特许经营进行维修。在Sokoto-Tambuwal-Jega-Kontagora-Makera公路方面，工程部记录显示第一期和第二期工程于2021年11月25日完成验收并移交。一个月后，2021年Sukuk招股说明书又为同一公路的第一段分配了15亿奈拉。招股说明书没有说明这笔资金是否用于支付已完工工程到期的款项，我们也未找到后来能够解释此事的官方记录。纳萨拉瓦州与贝努埃州之间的Loko-Oweto大桥于2023年5月23日通过线上启用仪式正式向公众开放。一年后，联邦工程部日期为2024年5月27日的在建项目记分卡仍将大桥及引道列为完成度95.19%。两份记录均来自政府，二者不可能都反映完整情况。有些债务甚至完全无法追溯到贷款。DMO于2026年6月30日发布的外债报告列出4笔合计9.125亿美元的款项，无法全部或大部分追溯至任何已公布的贷款协议、用途或条款。最大一笔是欠非洲进出口银行（Afreximbank）的8.3578亿美元，而三个月前为6.3782亿美元。2025年末的债务存量中，Afreximbank没有单独列项。还有一些筹措资金时没有项目清单。联邦政府5500亿奈拉的Sukuk，包括2023年发行额中工程部所占份额以及2025年发行额的全部，均未公布其用于支付哪些道路的清单。购买Sukuk的投资者会被告知其所依托的资产，而最终负责偿还的公民至少应获得同等程度的说明。……国民议会和各州议会应在批准新贷款前，要求查看以往贷款取得了何种成果。《财政责任法》已经要求说明用途；议员完全有理由询问上一次借款的用途是否得到实现……尼日利亚将继续借款，每个国家都是如此。以公众名义举债就意味着有义务向公众交代，而这一义务不会在贷款协议签署时终结。债务规模使这一切更加严重。2026年6月30日，公共债务总额为166.79万亿奈拉，而2016年末为17.36万亿奈拉。其中一部分增幅来自2023年对22.71万亿奈拉央行垫款（Ways and Means）的证券化，也有一部分来自奈拉贬值，但其余大部分是新增借款。如今有10个州的债务超过一整年的财政收入。卡杜纳州的债务相当于其2025年收入的336.7%，只有5个州及FCT处于财政责任委员会援引DMO数据所列50%指导线之内或以下。财政透明度与公共廉政中心（CeFTPI）曾两次致函DMO，指出其中一些风险信号并要求澄清。DMO确认收到函件，但迄今仍未回答所提出的问题。我们无意作最坏假设，其中一些款项很可能存在合理解释。然而，DMO正是应当能够告诉尼日利亚民众国家欠谁、为何借款以及借款条件为何的机构。采取几项措施就能带来很大改变。DMO应逐笔公布外债存量，列明每笔融资的贷款方、日期、条款和用途，并在重组各州债务时公布涉及的州和金额。每笔贷款和债券都应以一份独立于用款机构的公开完工记录收尾。包括联邦政府在内的债券发行方，应公布每期债券将资助的项目，并持续报告项目进展直至债券到期；不应将资金拨给官方记录已注明完工的工程。最后，国民议会和各州议会应在批准新贷款前，要求查看以往贷款取得了何种成果。《财政责任法》已经要求说明用途；议员完全有理由询问上一次借款的用途是否得到实现。尼日利亚将继续借款，每个国家都是如此。以公众名义举债就意味着有义务向公众交代，而这一义务不会在贷款协议签署时终结。Umar Yakubu是财政透明度与公共廉政中心执行主任

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/2.summary: The media office, which accused some governors of allegedly working behind the scenes to compromise the democratic process, said political leaders should focus on presenting their records of performance rather than seeking to retain power through electoral manipulation. “Instead of presenting their records of service, performance and achievements, they are turning to electoral manipulation and safeguards for rigging,” the statement alleged.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/2.summary_zh: 媒体办公室指控一些州长暗中破坏民主进程，并表示政治领导人应专注于展示自己的政绩，而不是试图通过操纵选举来保住权力。声明称：“他们没有展示自己的履职记录、政绩和成就，反而求助于操纵选举和为舞弊提供保障。”
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/2.body: • Accuses governors of prioritising political survival over performance • Insists leadership must be earned through service, not intimidation The Peter Obi Media Office has warned state governors against alleged attempts to manipulate the 2027 general election, declaring that Nigerians will resist any process that undermines the credibility of the polls. The media office, which accused some governors of allegedly working behind the scenes to compromise the democratic process, said political leaders should focus on presenting their records of performance rather than seeking to retain power through electoral manipulation. It maintained that any electoral process that failed to meet the standards of freedom, fairness and transparency would be rejected by Nigerians, who, it said, were determined to exercise their democratic rights. In a statement issued Tuesday by its spokesman, Indris Zekeri Jnr, the Peter Obi Media Office said governors should recognise that political leadership is a privilege earned through service and not an entitlement to be retained through deceit, intimidation or interference with elections. The statement, titled, ‘ Nigerians Will Choose the Best Product in the Marketplace,’ accused some governors of becoming increasingly desperate as the 2027 general election approaches. “Instead of presenting their records of service, performance and achievements, they are turning to electoral manipulation and safeguards for rigging,” the statement alleged. It warned that attempts to undermine the democratic process would not permanently suppress the will of the electorate, insisting that Nigerians had become increasingly determined to reject leaders they considered undeserving of another mandate. Part of the statement read: “The 2027 election will be a defining moment for our nation. Nigerians are resolved to reclaim their country through the power of their votes. The media office further argued that political leaders should be judged by their records and capacity to address the country’s challenges rather than their ability to deploy political influence to retain power. It also reiterated its position that Peter Obi remained a preferred choice among Nigerians, citing what it described as his commitment to competence, character, compassion and responsible leadership. According to the statement, Obi represents an alternative leadership proposition capable of addressing Nigeria’s challenges and restoring national dignity, prosperity and hope. The media office urged political officeholders to respect the sovereignty of the electorate, stressing that the authority to determine who governs the country ultimately rests with the people. It added that Nigerians were prepared to defend their votes in the 2027 elections, warning that electoral manipulation, intimidation and political manoeuvring would not override their democratic aspirations. “The mandate rests with the people. Nigeria must function again, and it will be OK,” the statement added. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/2.title_zh: 2027年：奥比警告州长不要操纵选举，称尼日利亚人民将抵制舞弊
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/03/2.body_zh:
• 指责州长把政治生存置于治理绩效之上 • 坚称领导权应通过服务而非恐吓来赢得

Peter Obi Media Office警告各州长不要图谋操纵2027年大选，并宣称尼日利亚人民将抵制任何损害选举可信度的程序。该媒体办公室指控一些州长暗中采取行动，破坏民主程序，并表示政治领导人应着重展示自己的施政记录，而不是通过操纵选举来维持权力。它坚持认为，任何未能达到自由、公平和透明标准的选举程序，都会遭到尼日利亚人民拒绝；该办公室称，尼日利亚人民决心行使自己的民主权利。

Peter Obi Media Office发言人Indris Zekeri Jnr于星期二发表声明称，州长们应当认识到，政治领导权是一项通过服务赢得的特权，而不是可以通过欺骗、恐吓或干预选举来保有的既得权利。声明题为《尼日利亚人民将选择市场上的最佳产品》，指控一些州长随着2027年大选临近而变得越来越绝望。

“这些州长没有展示自己在服务、绩效和成就方面的记录，反而求助于操纵选举以及为舞弊提供保障，”声明称。

声明警告称，破坏民主程序的企图无法永久压制选民的意志，并坚持认为，尼日利亚人民已越来越坚决地拒绝那些他们认为不配再次获得授权的领导人。

声明的一部分写道：“2027年大选将成为我国历史上的一个决定性时刻。尼日利亚人民决心通过选票的力量重新夺回自己的国家。

该媒体办公室进一步认为，政治领导人的评价标准应是他们的施政记录以及解决国家挑战的能力，而不是他们调动政治影响力维持权力的能力。它还重申了自己的立场，即Peter Obi仍是尼日利亚人民的首选之一，并援引其所称的Obi对能力、品格、同情心和负责任领导力的承诺。

根据该声明，Obi代表了一种不同于以往的领导模式，能够应对尼日利亚面临的挑战，并恢复国家尊严、繁荣与希望。该媒体办公室敦促政治公职人员尊重选民的主权，强调最终决定由谁治理国家的权力归根结底属于人民。它补充说，尼日利亚人民已准备好在2027年大选中捍卫自己的选票，并警告称，操纵选举、恐吓和政治操弄无法凌驾于他们的民主诉求之上。

“授权属于人民。尼日利亚必须再次正常运转，而且会好起来的，”声明补充道。

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body: Nearly 90 per cent of Nigerian adults support measures to reduce methane emissions, one of the most potent greenhouse gases contributing to global warming, a new survey has found. The figure represents a 17-percentage-point increase from the 72 per cent recorded in 2024. The survey also found that more than half (53 per cent) of Nigerian adults are very concerned about climate change. The Global Methane Hub (GMH) commissioned the survey in collaboration with the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication (YPCCC), and it was published on 29 October. Conducted across Nigeria and 17 other countries, the international survey sought to measure public awareness of climate change and methane emissions, and to examine attitudes towards solutions for reducing methane pollution. The findings show that concern is even greater regarding immediate environmental threats. About 67 per cent of Nigerian respondents said they were very concerned about poor water quality, while 60 per cent expressed similar concerns about flooding and access to drinking water. Another 55 per cent were very concerned about poor air quality. Researchers said the findings reflect the growing effects of climate change in Nigeria, where increasingly intense rainfall and flooding are putting communities, infrastructure and water systems at risk. The findings also reinforce concerns PREMIUM TIMES has repeatedly highlighted about methane emissions across Nigeria’s oil and gas sector and their consequences for the lives and livelihoods of communities in oil-producing areas. Nigeria faces significant methane emission challenges, largely driven by oil and gas production, routine gas flaring, venting and ageing infrastructure. Concerns have also persisted over the enforcement of regulations governing gas flaring and methane emissions. Methane leaks and routine gas flaring in the Niger Delta have been linked to environmental pollution, contamination of local water sources, damage to farmlands and respiratory health risks. In Bille, Rivers State, for instance, severe methane bubbling and contamination of water wells have reportedly created acute health and safety concerns for residents. The continued burning and venting of associated gas also represents a significant economic loss, as billions of cubic feet of gas that could otherwise be captured and commercialised are wasted annually. In July, heavy rainfall triggered widespread flooding across parts of Nigeria, including Lagos, as saturated soils increased the risk of flash floods. Authorities also warned that 27 states could be affected. As the rainy season intensified, authorities subsequently placed 14 states on flood alert, highlighting the growing risks facing communities already struggling with flooding, deteriorating water quality and limited access to safe drinking water. Methane is a short-lived climate pollutant and one of the most effective targets for slowing global warming in the near term. It is more than 80 times as potent as carbon dioxide over 20 years. Reducing methane emissions can also deliver significant public health and economic benefits, including improved air quality and reduced pollution exposure. “As flooding and water challenges put greater pressure on communities across Nigeria, the case for tackling methane is becoming increasingly clear,” said Marcelo Mena, Chief Executive Officer of the Global Methane Hub. “This survey shows strong and growing support for methane action, with nearly nine in ten Nigerians now supporting efforts to reduce emissions. In the oil and gas sector, for example, cutting methane leaks, venting and flaring reduces pollution and safety risks for nearby communities while helping slow warming. Tengi George-Ikoli, Nigeria Country Manager at the Natural Resource Governance Institute (NRGI), said Nigerians had legitimate reasons to be concerned about methane emissions and their effects on health, the environment and livelihoods. “Nigerians are right to be concerned about methane emissions and the harm they cause to health, environments and livelihoods,” she said. “In parts of the Niger Delta, those costs are already being felt, so communities are justified in calling for stronger enforcement of environmental regulations and for clear mechanisms to prevent, mitigate and respond to methane-related harm. Anthony Leiserowitz, Director of the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication, said understanding public awareness and perceptions was essential to effective communication and policymaking. “Understanding what people know and think is essential to effective public communication and policymaking,” he said. “Methane reduction is one of the fastest ways to limit global warming, making it critical that the public understands both the challenge and the solutions. The survey found that 69 per cent of Nigerian respondents believe climate change is caused by human activities, while 89 per cent support measures to reduce methane emissions. It also found that nearly two-thirds (64 per cent) of respondents were familiar with methane. Oil and gas companies were identified as both significant contributors to climate change and important actors capable of addressing it. About 57 per cent of respondents ranked oil and gas companies among the three entities most responsible for climate change, while 78 per cent considered them very capable of making meaningful changes. The findings show broad support for reducing methane emissions across the three major sectors responsible for most human-caused methane pollution: agriculture, waste and energy. In agriculture, 84 per cent of respondents supported efforts to minimise methane emissions, while 88 per cent backed measures to reduce emissions from waste disposal. Similarly, 88 per cent supported reducing methane emissions from energy production. Overall, the 89 per cent support for methane reduction matched the proportion of respondents who backed broader climate action. The report said the findings demonstrate widespread public support for industry-led interventions and stronger environmental protections. It also noted that Nigerians see corruption as a major obstacle to enforcing environmental regulations effectively. With strong majorities supporting methane reduction across all three sectors, the report said policymakers and industries have an opportunity to advance solutions that reduce pollution while strengthening environmental accountability. The international survey covered 18 countries across four continents: Brazil, China, Denmark, Ethiopia, Germany, Greece, Indonesia, Italy, Malaysia, Morocco, Nigeria, Paraguay, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and Uruguay. The online survey gathered responses from 12,189 adults, including at least 700 respondents in Nigeria. Participants were asked questions about their perceptions of climate change, environmental concerns, awareness of methane emissions and support for specific policies to reduce methane pollution. Across the countries surveyed, 85 per cent of respondents supported action to reduce methane emissions, indicating widespread international backing for efforts to tackle the pollutant. Support was particularly strong in Asia, Africa and Latin America, reaching 94 per cent in South Korea, 91 per cent in Malaysia, 90 per cent in China and Brazil, and 89 per cent in Nigeria and South Africa. The findings also showed that respondents who reported experiencing greater climate change impacts were more likely to support measures to reduce methane emissions. Across regions, respondents expressed concern about the tangible effects of climate change in their communities, including extreme heat, wildfires, drought, flooding and deteriorating water quality. Waste emerged as a particularly prominent area for methane reduction in several countries, alongside strong support for interventions in the energy and agriculture sectors. The report further highlighted public expectations for governments and industries to take greater responsibility for reducing methane emissions. The report described methane reduction as one of the fastest ways to slow global warming in the near term. Methane accounts for approximately 30 per cent of the warming experienced since pre-industrial times and is more than 80 times as powerful as carbon dioxide over 20 years. Unlike carbon dioxide, which can remain in the atmosphere for centuries, most methane breaks down within approximately a decade. According to the report, cutting human-caused methane emissions by 45 per cent this decade could prevent nearly 0.3 degrees Celsius of warming by 2045, helping to keep international climate commitments within reach. Reducing methane emissions would also improve air quality, protect agricultural production, create jobs, strengthen food systems, reduce health risks, and improve community resilience. The report stressed that because methane pollution crosses national borders, coordinated action among governments, businesses, researchers and communities is essential to achieving significant reductions. Melissa Bell, Senior Vice President of Research at Global Strategy Group, GMH’s research partner, said the consistent findings across countries demonstrated sustained public support for methane reduction. “The consistency of these findings sends a clear signal: support for reducing methane emissions is strong and sustained,” she said. Global Strategy Group conducted the 10-minute online survey between 3 and 25 August 2026. The questionnaire was translated into 13 languages and administered across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia. Responses were collected from adults aged 18 and above who currently reside in the participating countries and have internet access. The researchers applied weights for age, gender, geographical location, and education to ensure the samples represented adults with internet access in each country. At least 700 responses were collected in 15 countries, including Nigeria, South Africa, China, Indonesia, Malaysia, South Korea, Morocco, Brazil, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Germany, Greece, Spain, Italy and the United Arab Emirates. The margin of error was ±3.7 per cent in these countries, except Morocco and Brazil, where it was ±3.6 per cent. In Ethiopia, Paraguay and Uruguay, at least 400 responses were collected, with margins of error of ±4.9 per cent, ±4.5 per cent and ±3.9 per cent, respectively
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title_zh: 近90%的尼日利亚成年人支持削减甲烷排放
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body_zh: 一项新调查显示，近90%的尼日利亚成年人支持采取措施减少甲烷排放。甲烷是加剧全球变暖的温室气体中危害最大的一类。该比例较2024年记录的72%上升了17个百分点。调查还发现，超过一半（53%）的尼日利亚成年人对气候变化非常担忧。全球甲烷中心（GMH）委托耶鲁气候变化传播项目（YPCCC）开展这项调查，并于10月29日公布结果。这项国际调查在尼日利亚及其他17个国家进行，旨在了解公众对气候变化和甲烷排放的认知，并考察公众对减少甲烷污染解决方案的态度。调查结果显示，公众对眼前环境威胁的担忧程度更高。约67%的尼日利亚受访者表示非常担忧水质恶劣，60%的受访者对洪灾和饮用水获取问题表达了同样的担忧。另有55%的受访者非常担忧空气质量不佳。研究人员表示，这些发现反映了气候变化在尼日利亚日益加剧的影响。当地降雨强度不断上升，洪水频发，使社区、基础设施和供水系统面临风险。这些发现也进一步印证了PREMIUM TIMES多次报道的担忧，即尼日利亚石油和天然气行业产生的甲烷排放及其对产油区社区生活和生计造成的后果。尼日利亚面临严重的甲烷排放挑战，主要由石油和天然气生产、日常天然气燃烧、排放以及老化基础设施所致。有关天然气燃烧和甲烷排放法规执行不力的问题也持续存在。尼日尔三角洲的甲烷泄漏和日常天然气燃烧已被证实与环境污染、当地水源污染、农田受损和呼吸系统健康风险有关。例如，在河流州比莱，严重的甲烷冒泡和水井污染据报已对居民造成紧迫的健康与安全问题。相关天然气持续燃烧和排放还会造成重大经济损失，每年数十亿立方英尺本可收集并进行商业利用的天然气被白白浪费。7月，强降雨引发尼日利亚部分地区大范围洪灾，拉各斯也在其中，土壤含水量饱和增加了山洪暴发风险。当局还警告称，27个州可能受到影响。随着雨季加剧，当局随后将14个州列为洪灾预警州，凸显出相关社区正面临日益严峻的风险，而这些社区已在洪灾、水质恶化和安全饮用水获取受限等问题上苦苦挣扎。甲烷是一种短寿命气候污染物，也是短期内减缓全球变暖最有效的治理目标之一。按20年尺度计算，其温室效应强度是二氧化碳的80多倍。减少甲烷排放还能带来显著的公共卫生和经济益处，包括改善空气质量、降低污染暴露。全球甲烷中心首席执行官Marcelo Mena表示：“随着洪灾和水资源问题给尼日利亚各地社区带来更大压力，解决甲烷问题的理由正变得越来越明确。这项调查显示，公众对采取甲烷行动的支持强劲且不断上升，目前近十分之九的尼日利亚人支持减少排放的努力。例如，在石油和天然气行业，减少甲烷泄漏、排放和燃烧，既能降低附近社区面临的污染与安全风险，也有助于减缓全球变暖。”自然资源治理研究所（NRGI）尼日利亚国家经理Tengi George-Ikoli表示，尼日利亚人有充分理由担忧甲烷排放及其对健康、环境和生计造成的影响。她说：“尼日利亚人担忧甲烷排放及其对健康、环境和生计造成的危害是理所当然的。在尼日尔三角洲部分地区，这些代价已经显现，因此社区要求加强环境法规执行，并建立明确机制来防范、减轻和应对甲烷相关危害，是完全合理的。”耶鲁气候变化传播项目主任Anthony Leiserowitz表示，了解公众的认知和看法对于有效沟通和制定政策至关重要。他说：“了解人们知道什么、如何看待问题，是有效开展公众沟通和制定政策的关键。减少甲烷是限制全球变暖最快的方式之一，因此让公众充分理解挑战与解决方案至关重要。调查发现，69%的尼日利亚受访者认为气候变化由人类活动引起，89%支持采取措施减少甲烷排放。调查还发现，近三分之二（64%）的受访者熟悉甲烷。石油和天然气公司既被视为气候变化的重要促成者，也被视为有能力解决这一问题的重要行动方。约57%的受访者将石油和天然气公司列为对气候变化负有最大责任的三类主体之一，78%的受访者则认为这些公司非常有能力推动实质性改变。调查结果显示，公众广泛支持在造成大部分人为甲烷污染的三大行业——农业、废物处理和能源——减少甲烷排放。在农业领域，84%的受访者支持努力将甲烷排放降至最低水平，88%支持采取措施减少废物处理产生的排放。同样，88%的受访者支持减少能源生产产生的甲烷排放。总体而言，支持减少甲烷的89%与支持更广泛气候行动的受访者比例相当。报告称，这些发现表明，公众广泛支持由行业主导采取干预措施并加强环境保护。报告还指出，尼日利亚人将腐败视为有效执行环境法规的一大障碍。报告称，在所有三大行业中，减少甲烷均获得大多数人的强烈支持，政策制定者和各行业因此有机会推动既能减少污染、又能加强环境问责的解决方案。这项国际调查覆盖四大洲的18个国家：巴西、中国、丹麦、埃塞俄比亚、德国、希腊、印度尼西亚、意大利、马来西亚、摩洛哥、尼日利亚、巴拉圭、南非、韩国、西班牙、阿联酋、英国和乌拉圭。这项在线调查共收集12,189名成年人的回答，其中尼日利亚至少有700名受访者。参与者就其对气候变化的看法、环境担忧、对甲烷排放的认知，以及对减少甲烷污染的特定政策的支持情况回答了问题。在所有受访国家中，85%的受访者支持采取行动减少甲烷排放，表明国际社会广泛支持应对这一污染物。亚洲、非洲和拉丁美洲的支持率尤其高，韩国达到94%，马来西亚为91%，中国和巴西均为90%，尼日利亚和南非均为89%。调查还显示，报告经历更大气候变化影响的受访者更有可能支持减少甲烷排放的措施。各地区受访者均对气候变化给社区造成的实际影响表示担忧，包括极端高温、野火、干旱、洪灾和水质恶化。在多个国家，废物处理成为减少甲烷排放的突出领域，同时公众也强烈支持在能源和农业领域采取干预措施。报告进一步强调，公众期望政府和各行业承担更大责任，减少甲烷排放。报告指出，减少甲烷是短期内减缓全球变暖最快的方式之一。自工业革命前以来，全球变暖幅度中约有30%由甲烷造成；按20年尺度计算，其作用强度是二氧化碳的80多倍。与可以在大气中存留数百年的二氧化碳不同，大多数甲烷会在约十年内分解。报告称，如果本十年将人为甲烷排放削减45%，到2045年可避免近0.3摄氏度的升温，从而帮助国际气候承诺维持在可实现范围内。减少甲烷排放还将改善空气质量、保护农业生产、创造就业、加强粮食体系、降低健康风险，并增强社区韧性。报告强调，由于甲烷污染会跨越国界，各政府、企业、研究人员和社区协调行动对于实现显著减排至关重要。GMH研究合作方Global Strategy Group研究高级副总裁Melissa Bell表示，各国得出的结论具有一致性，说明公众对减少甲烷排放的支持持续存在。她说：“这些调查结果的一致性传递了一个明确信号：公众对减少甲烷排放的支持强劲且持续。”Global Strategy Group于2026年8月3日至25日开展了这项为期10分钟的在线调查。问卷被翻译成13种语言，在欧洲、南美洲、非洲和亚洲实施。调查收集了目前居住在参与国、年龄在18岁及以上且能够上网的成年人的回答。研究人员根据年龄、性别、地理位置和教育程度进行加权，以确保样本能够代表各国可上网的成年人。尼日利亚、南非、中国、印度尼西亚、马来西亚、韩国、摩洛哥、巴西、丹麦、英国、德国、希腊、西班牙、意大利和阿联酋等15个国家各收集至少700份回答。这些国家的误差范围为±3.7%，但摩洛哥和巴西为±3.6%。埃塞俄比亚、巴拉圭和乌拉圭各收集至少400份回答，误差范围分别为±4.9%、±4.5%和±3.9%。

Caverton Offshore Support Group dropped 7.58 percent to close at N3.05 and Livestock Feeds declined by 6.51 percent to close at N13.65, per share. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nige.summary: The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has said the country’s exports increased by more than 25 per cent in the last two years, attributing the growth to Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port operators. He said Nigeria’s population and economic potential gave it an advantage over other countries in West and Central Africa, adding that recent reforms had also improved cargo throughput at the nation’s ports.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nige.summary_zh: 尼日利亚港务局（NPA）表示，过去两年该国出口增长超过25%，并将这一增长归因于联邦政府的改革以及与港口运营商协作的改善。他说，尼日利亚的人口和经济潜力使该国相较于西非和中非其他国家具有优势，并补充说，近期改革也提高了全国港口的货物吞吐量。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nige.body: The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has said the country’s exports increased by more than 25 per cent in the last two years, attributing the growth to Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port operators. The Managing Director of NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, disclosed this while speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH). He said Nigeria’s population and economic potential gave it an advantage over other countries in West and Central Africa, adding that recent reforms had also improved cargo throughput at the nation’s ports. Dantsoho said the export growth was not limited to oil and gas but extended to manufacturing and agricultural products, including cocoa, cashew and other raw materials. “Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. And then these are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In terms of oil and gas, like I mentioned, we are doing fantastically around that, but then also in the other areas of manufacturing and agriculture, you know, raw materials like cocoa, like cashew and all that. Volumes have increased,” he said. He attributed the growth partly to the partnership between the NPA and major terminal operators, particularly APM Terminals. The NPA chief said the authority had put measures in place to sustain the growth, including the establishment of Export Processing Terminals to facilitate the handling and documentation of export cargoes. He disclosed that about four such terminals were operating in Nigeria, with the NPA collaborating with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargoes were processed locally and met required standards before shipment. Dantsoho said the reforms had also positioned Nigeria to take greater advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), particularly through increased trade with other African countries. He cited Nigeria’s engagement with Morocco, which he described as a growing manufacturing hub for electric and other vehicles, as an example of opportunities for cooperation. The NPA managing director also attributed Nigeria’s improved performance in global port rankings to increased efficiency, technology adoption and collaboration with industry stakeholders. He said two Nigerian ports featured among the top 20 in the latest World Bank global ports ranking. Dantsoho further disclosed that revenue generated from ports across the country had quadrupled, alongside an increase in cargo volumes. He said the authority was monitoring port performance across West and Central Africa through a regional dashboard, adding that the data showed improvements in Nigeria’s port efficiency as well as progress in countries such as Tanzania and Kenya. According to him, the NPA plans to sustain partnerships with major industry players in countries including Morocco and South Africa to improve port operations and regional trade. On infrastructure development, Dantsoho said the Federal Government was planning to invest $1 billion in the expansion and modernisation of Apapa Port as part of its medium- to long-term strategy. He said the project would require substantial private-sector participation, adding that the NPA was working with APM Terminals and other investors to mobilise the required capital. The authority was also pursuing technology partnerships to improve port operations, he said. Dantsoho disclosed that the NPA had partnered with a Singaporean firm to develop a single-window system, while discussions were ongoing with a company from Abu Dhabi to develop a port community system. He said the initiatives were expected to improve coordination among port stakeholders, simplify processes and enhance efficiency. Comments expressed here do not reflect the opinions of Vanguard newspapers or any employee thereof
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nige.title_zh: 尼日利亚出口额两年内增长25%
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/nige.body_zh: 尼日利亚港务局（NPA）表示，过去两年该国出口增长超过25%，并将这一增长归因于联邦政府的改革以及与港口运营商合作得到改善。NPA总经理阿布巴卡尔·丹措霍博士在伦敦举行的年度世界港口大会上透露了上述情况。此次大会由国际港口和港湾协会（IAPH）组织。他说，尼日利亚的人口和经济潜力使该国相较于西非和中非其他国家具有优势，近期改革也提高了全国港口的货物吞吐量。丹措霍表示，出口增长不仅限于石油和天然气，还延伸至制造产品和农产品，包括可可、腰果及其他原材料。他说：“从统计上看，过去两年尼日利亚的出口增长了25%。而且这些出口并非主要依靠石油和天然气。在石油和天然气方面，正如我提到的，我们取得了极其显著的成绩，但在制造和农业等其他领域也实现了增长，例如可可、腰果等原材料。货运量已经增加。”他指出，出口增长部分得益于NPA与主要码头运营商，尤其是APM Terminals之间的合作。这名NPA负责人表示，该局已采取措施维持增长势头，包括设立出口加工码头，以便利出口货物的装卸和单证办理。他透露，尼日利亚目前约有4座此类码头正在运营，NPA正与码头运营商、尼日利亚海关总署及其他相关机构合作，确保出口货物在当地完成处理，并在装运前符合规定标准。丹措霍表示，改革还使尼日利亚能够更加充分地利用非洲大陆自由贸易区（AfCFTA）的优势，尤其是通过增加与其他非洲国家的贸易额。他以尼日利亚与摩洛哥的合作为例，称摩洛哥正日益发展成为电动车辆及其他车辆的制造中心，并认为这体现了合作机会。NPA总经理还表示，效率提高、技术应用以及与行业利益相关方加强合作，使尼日利亚在全球港口排名中的表现有所改善。他说，在最新的世界银行全球港口排名中，有2座尼日利亚港口跻身前20名。丹措霍进一步透露，随着货运量增加，全国各港口产生的收入增长了4倍。他说，该局通过一个区域性仪表板监测西非和中非各地的港口表现，数据显示尼日利亚港口效率有所提高，坦桑尼亚和肯尼亚等国家也取得进展。据他介绍，NPA计划与摩洛哥和南非等国家的行业主要企业保持合作，以改善港口运营并促进区域贸易。在基础设施开发方面，丹措霍表示，作为其中长期战略的一部分，联邦政府计划投资10亿美元扩建和现代化改造阿帕帕港。他说，该项目需要私营部门大力参与，NPA正与APM Terminals及其他投资者合作，以筹集所需资本。他表示，该局还在寻求技术合作伙伴关系，以改善港口运营。丹措霍透露，NPA已与一家新加坡公司合作开发单一窗口系统，同时正与阿布扎比的一家公司商谈开发港口社区系统。他说，预计这些举措将改善港口各利益相关方之间的协调，简化流程并提高效率。此处发表的意见不代表Vanguard报纸或其任何员工的观点

https://leadership.ng/stop-saying-there-.title: “Stop Saying There Is Hunger In Nigeria” — Wike’s Aide Tells Gen Zs
https://leadership.ng/stop-saying-there-.summary: Olayinka said Nigeria had made progress over the years, particularly in leveraging technology to create jobs and enable people to earn a living through digital platforms and social media. The FCT minister’s aide also questioned what he described as the persistent narrative that Nigerians were experiencing hunger, arguing that economic hardship should not overshadow evidence of individual enterprise and development.
https://leadership.ng/stop-saying-there-.summary_zh: 奥拉扬卡表示，多年来尼日利亚取得了进展，尤其是在利用技术创造就业机会，以及让人们通过数字平台和社交媒体谋生方面。联邦首都特区部长的助手还质疑了他所称的“尼日利亚人正在遭受饥饿”的持续叙事，认为经济困难不应掩盖个人创业和发展所取得的成果。
https://leadership.ng/stop-saying-there-.body: Olayinka said Nigeria had made progress over the years, particularly in leveraging technology to create jobs and enable people to earn a living through digital platforms and social media. He made the remarks while speaking on Democracy Today , a programme on the African Independent Television (AIT). According to him, some young Nigerians perceive the country’s economic situation differently because they grew up depending on their parents for basic needs and are only now experiencing the challenges of providing for themselves. He said, “When they were growing up, they didn’t know how Nigeria was. Their parents were providing for them. Now they have seen; they have to provide for themselves.” Olayinka argued that despite the economic difficulties Nigerians are experiencing, the country has recorded improvements, particularly in technology and the opportunities it offers individuals to earn income. He illustrated the changes by comparing the challenges journalists faced in transmitting news reports in the past with the ease of sharing content through digital platforms today. “Imagine when you started journalism now, for you to send your story, do you know how… Technology has made a lot of things a lot different,” he said. Recounting his experience in the media industry, Olayinka explained that journalists previously had to travel long distances to transmit television reports, sometimes relying on physical tapes and transport services to deliver their work to broadcast stations. “For us to send visuals, when I was working with… I know I used to travel by road from Bauchi to Jos to be able to uplink the stories,” he said. The presidential aide said technological advancement had since transformed how people work and earn money, noting that individuals could now create digital content, livestream, and earn income from home. “Now, technology has even provided jobs for a lot of people, things that were not available to us growing up. I know people now that sit in their house, do content, be on one social media app, do live streaming, they get money,” he said. The FCT minister’s aide also questioned what he described as the persistent narrative that Nigerians were experiencing hunger, arguing that economic hardship should not overshadow evidence of individual enterprise and development. “Let us not keep this mindset of telling people there is hunger, there is hunger, there is hunger,” he said. He further cited people building houses and engaging in economic activities as examples of Nigerians making progress despite prevailing concerns about the cost of living. Olayinka also noted that homelessness existed in developed countries, arguing that economic difficulties were not exclusive to Nigeria. He maintained that the government’s primary responsibility was to create an enabling environment for citizens to pursue economic opportunities and improve their livelihoods. “The only thing the government can do is to provide an enabling environment,” he said. His comments come amid ongoing public concerns over the cost of living, food affordability, and the economic challenges facing households across Nigeria. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/stop-saying-there-.title_zh: “别再说尼日利亚有人挨饿”——维克顾问敦促Z世代
https://leadership.ng/stop-saying-there-.body_zh: 奥拉辛卡表示，多年来尼日利亚取得了进展，尤其是在利用技术创造就业机会，以及让人们通过数字平台和社交媒体谋生方面。他是在非洲独立电视台（AIT）的《今日民主》节目中发表上述言论的。据他所说，一些尼日利亚年轻人对本国经济状况的看法有所不同，因为他们从小依靠父母满足基本需求，如今才切身体会到自立更生的挑战。他说：“他们成长的时候，并不知道尼日利亚是什么样子。他们的父母会供养他们。如今他们已经看到了，必须自己养活自己。”奥拉辛卡认为，尽管尼日利亚人正经历经济困难，但国家仍取得了改善，尤其是在技术发展以及技术为个人创造收入机会方面。他通过对比过去记者传输新闻报道所面临的困难与如今通过数字平台分享内容的便利，说明了这些变化。他说：“想象一下，如果你们现在刚开始从事新闻工作，要发出一篇报道，你知道那有多……技术让许多事情发生了巨大的变化。”奥拉辛卡回顾自己在媒体行业的经历，称记者过去往往需要长途跋涉才能传输电视报道，有时还要依靠实体磁带及运输服务，将工作成果送至播映机构。他说：“我们要把画面传送出去。我还在……工作的时候时，记得我曾从包奇乘车到乔斯，才能把这些报道上传传送。”这位总统助理表示，技术进步此后改变了人们工作和赚钱的方式，并指出如今人们可以在家中制作数字内容、开展直播并获得收入。他说：“如今，技术甚至为许多人提供了工作，这些都是我们成长时没有的。我知道现在有些人足不出户，制作内容，使用一个社交媒体应用进行直播，就能赚到钱。”联邦首都 Territory 部长的助理还质疑了他所称的、一直存在的“尼日利亚人正在挨饿”这一叙事，认为经济困难不应掩盖个人进取和发展的证据。他说：“我们不要一直抱着这种心态，对人们说挨饿、挨饿、挨饿。”他还列举了建房和从事经济活动的人，称他们证明尼日利亚人尽管面临生活成本等普遍担忧，仍在取得进展。奥拉辛卡还指出，发达国家同样存在无家可归现象，经济困难并非尼日利亚独有。他坚持认为，政府的首要责任是为公民创造有利环境，使其能够寻求经济机会、改善生计。他说：“政府唯一能做的，就是提供有利环境。”他的言论是在公众持续关注生活成本、食品负担能力以及尼日利亚各地家庭面临的经济挑战之际发表的。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、独家内幕和独特视角将直接送达你的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入 LEADERSHIP NEWS 的 WhatsApp，随时随地获取全天候最新消息 →

https://www.politico.eu/article/greenlan.body: U.S. President Donald Trump called Greenland the greatest gift the United States had ever received in a call to Fox News on Tuesday. “Remember, [Europe] just gave the United States the greatest gift we were ever given. Do you know what it was? Greenland. We just got Greenland, you know that, right?” he said during a broadcast about Tuesday’s midterm elections, which was reshared on X by the U.S. State Department. Someone else on the call quickly clarified that Trump was referring to “a military deal.” Until September, Trump had repeatedly pushed for the U.S. to take control of the large, mineral-rich island, which is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, citing national security reasons. His fixation on the idea, and his repeated refusals to rule out using military force to take the territory — as well as his use of tariffs against allied countries he saw as standing in his way — stretched the NATO alliance close to breaking point . At NATO’s annual summit in July, Trump said the island “should be controlled by the United States, not by Denmark,” provoking warnings from European leaders who maintain the territory is not for sale and that its future should be left to its people. In September, Trump signed a defense agreement with the prime ministers of Greenland and Denmark, ending the stand-off. The deal expands U.S. military access and presence, and effectively grants NATO countries exclusivity on mining, while recognizing Denmark’s sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination. American voters head to the polls on Tuesday for the midterm elections. During the call, Trump said he thinks the results will be “better than you think.” Democrats are widely expected to make gains against the president’s Republican party
https://www.politico.eu/article/greenlan.title_zh: 特朗普称欧洲将格陵兰岛赠予美国，是“有史以来最伟大的礼物”
https://www.politico.eu/article/greenlan.body_zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周二接受福克斯新闻采访时，称格陵兰是美国收到过的最great礼物。特朗普在一次关于周二中期选举的直播节目中说：“记住，[欧洲]刚刚给了美国一份我们收到过的最伟大的礼物。你知道是什么吗？格陵兰。我们刚刚得到了格陵兰，你知道的，对吧？”美国国务院随后在X上转发了这段内容。通话中的另一位人士迅速澄清，特朗普所说的实际上是“一项军事协议”。直到9月，特朗普一直以国家安全为由，推动美国控制这个矿产丰富的大型岛屿。该岛是丹麦王国内部的自治领地。他对这一构想的执着，以及他一再拒绝排除动用武力夺取该领土的可能性，再加上他对那些他认为妨碍自己的盟国实施关税，使北约联盟一度濒临破裂。在7月举行的北约年度峰会上，特朗普称该岛“应由美国控制，而不是由丹麦控制”，引发欧洲领导人警告。他们坚持认为，该领土不出售，其未来应交由当地居民决定。9月，特朗普与格陵兰和丹麦的总理签署了一项防务协议，结束了对峙。这项协议扩大了美国对该地区的军事准入和驻军存在，并实际上赋予北约国家独家采矿权，同时承认丹麦的主权以及格陵兰人的自决权。美国选民周二前往投票站参加中期选举。通话中，特朗普表示，他认为选举结果将“比你想象的更好”。外界普遍预计，民主党将在这场选举中从总统所属的共和党手中夺回部分席位

https://www.myjoyonline.com/e-jobs4all-o.body: Applications have opened for the Entrepreneurship Jobs for All (E-Jobs4All) programme, a fully funded initiative designed to equip aspiring and existing entrepreneurs in Ghana with business development skills, mentorship and access to investment opportunities. The programme is a partnership between Queen’s University in Canada, the Community and Entrepreneurial Development Initiative (CEDI Ghana) and Leadogo Incorporated, Canada. It seeks to support startups, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), students, unemployed persons and fresh graduates interested in establishing or expanding their businesses. Under the initiative, participants will receive entrepreneurship and innovation training through the Dunin-Deshpande Innovation Centre at Queen’s University. They will also benefit from advisory and mentorship services provided by experts from Leadogo Incorporated and the PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) network. The programme will offer participants opportunities to pitch their business ideas to potential investors, alongside masterclasses, lecture series and networking opportunities with established entrepreneurs and business leaders. Successful participants who complete all three courses will receive a Certificate of Specialisation in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, as well as a micro-credential from Queen’s University. The programme is open to individuals committed to establishing or scaling up a business. Applicants must have basic English language proficiency and be willing to participate in virtual training sessions. Registration is free, with tuition fees at Queen’s University and mentorship and coaching fees from Leadogo Incorporated fully covered under the scholarship arrangement. Applications opened on November 1, 2026, and will close on November 30, 2026. Successful applicants are expected to register for courses between January 11 and 15, 2027, ahead of lectures and masterclasses scheduled to run from January 18 to August 30, 2027. https://www.myjoyonline.com/e-jobs4all-o.body_zh: 加纳“全民创业就业”（E-Jobs4All）计划现已开放申请。这是一项全额资助的计划，旨在帮助加纳有志创业者和现有创业者提升商业发展技能、获得指导，并获得投资机会。该计划由加拿大的女王大学、社区与企业发展倡议（CEDI Ghana）和加拿大的 Leadogo Incorporated 合作开展，旨在支持有意创办或扩展业务的初创企业、小型和中型企业（SMEs）、学生、失业人员和应届毕业生。根据该计划，参与者将通过女王大学的邓宁-德什潘德创新中心接受创业与创新培训。他们还将获得 Leadogo Incorporated 及 PricewaterhouseCoopers（PwC）网络专家提供的咨询和指导服务。该计划将让参与者有机会向潜在投资者推介商业创意，并参加大师课、系列讲座以及与成熟创业者和商业领袖交流的联谊活动。完成全部三门课程的优秀参与者将获得创业与创新专业证书，以及女王大学颁发的微证书。计划面向致力于创办企业或扩大业务规模的个人开放。申请者必须具备基本英语能力，并愿意参加线上培训课程。注册免费；根据奖学金安排，女王大学的学费以及 Leadogo Incorporated 的指导和辅导费用均全额获得资助。申请于2026年11月1日开放，将于2026年11月30日截止。获选申请者预计须在2027年1月11日至15日期间完成课程注册，随后参加定于2027年1月18日至8月30日举行的讲座和大师课。该计划预计将帮助创业者获得国际专业指导、实用商业知识以及潜在融资机会，以支持加纳企业发展和就业创造。

https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/w.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Weeks before the expiry of the Ganga Water Treaty in December, the Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) reiterated that India and Bangladesh have a “structured mechanism” to deal with the treaty’s requirements. Addressing the bi-weekly media briefing, MEA official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated that India has invited Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to visit New Delhi but that there is neither any “update” on the treaty’s renewal nor on the dates for the trip. Also read | Ganga Water Treaty is ‘flawed’, needs to be updated: Bangladesh river expert “Between India and Bangladesh, we have a Joint Rivers Commission which is the structured mechanism for discussion on all cross-boundary rivers, including the Ganga,” said Mr. Jaiswal, adding that India wishes to have a “positive relationship” with Bangladesh. The bilateral Ganga Water Treaty is set to expire on December 12. The treaty was signed in 1996 between India and Bangladesh when Sheikh Hasina of Awami League became Bangladesh’s Prime Minister for the first time. The three-decade old agreement for river water sharing requires expert-level and political consultations for renewing the pact. It is understood that since the treaty was signed at the level of Prime Ministers (Ms. Hasina and then Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda), a renewal of the agreement would happen at a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. However, Mr. Rahman who has visited China, Japan, Malaysia and the United States so far, has not yet responded to the invites from India though he was invited to both bilateral and multilateral events during the BRICS Summit in New Delhi in September. “As far as India-Bangladesh relationship is concerned we want to work towards a positive, forward looking and constructive relation,” said Mr. Jaiswal reiterating India’s invites to Prime Minister Rahman. Diplomatic sources from the Bangladeshi side had informed earlier that they are expecting an automatic short-term renewal of the treaty after the expiry on December 12, though the Indian officials have not indicated at that till now. Mr. Jaiswal also took note of the protests by the readymade garment industry workers in Bangladesh who have been hitting the streets demanding fair wages as the country faces high inflation and electricity crisis. “Yes, we have been following the situation in Bangladesh. There have been developments there and we will continue to follow the developments,” he said in response to a question on the protests by the workers in the garments sector. https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/0.summary: Nearly five years into the full-scale war, Russia’s military increasingly depends on foreign recruits. But for foreign recruits, who may number as high as 27,000, desertion comes with its own unique challenges. Now living outside Russia after deserting just over two months ago, his situation is bleak.
https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/0.summary_zh: 全面战争爆发近五年来，俄罗斯军队日益依赖外国招募人员。然而，对于人数可能高达27,000人的外国招募人员而言，逃兵问题也带来了独特的挑战。他两个多月前逃离俄罗斯，如今生活在俄罗斯境外，处境十分 bleak。
https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/0.body: Peter, a 24-year-old man from Pakistan, moved to Russia to study medicine in 2020. Four years later, he’d be lying on a hospital bed with stitches in his feet, the result of being caught in an explosion on the front lines in Ukraine. “When I signed the contract, I didn’t know this would happen,” he said of his experience fighting for the Russian military in a recent interview from a different country, requesting to use a pseudonym due to safety concerns. “I wouldn’t have signed it for any amount, for any passport.” Like tens of thousands of other foreigners, Peter went to Russia in search of a better life. Instead, he says, he found only misery after being deceived into joining the military to help Moscow wage its brutal war of aggression against Ukraine. Nearly five years into the full-scale war, Russia’s military increasingly depends on foreign recruits. But as the conflict drags on, they’ve joined their fellow Russian combatants in deserting from their units, a desperate and often harrowing decision. The risks for all deserters are steep. If caught, they face up to 10 years in Russian prison. But for foreign recruits, who may number as high as 27,000, desertion comes with its own unique challenges. Many face legal persecution in their home countries, an international system that is reluctant to help and staggering uncertainty. Peter’s story shares similarities with those of others who came to Russia and joined the military: limited options at home, the promise of unbridled opportunity in a major global power, a shady recruiter, a battlefield injury and a desperate escape. During two interviews with The Moscow Times, Peter described an experience that divided his life into before and after, derailing any semblance of a plan for his future. He asked that some details about his story be withheld due to security concerns, but provided documentation to support his claims, including a copy of his military contract, medical records and photos from his time serving. Originally from a small city in Pakistan, Peter always knew he wanted to be a doctor. It’s a profession that runs in the family. But when it came time to begin his studies, the price of education in his home country was too steep. He found a promising opportunity abroad: a university in Krasnodar, the large southern Russian city located some 200 kilometers (124 miles) west of annexed Crimea, where he could get a medical degree for an affordable price. He arrived in 2020. Peter enjoyed his time in Russia. In between making friends and learning the language, he contemplated a future in which his degree afforded him options in Russia or elsewhere. But when his family told him they could no longer send financial support, his education was thrown into doubt. That was when a friend, also a medical student in Krasnodar, told him about a way he could make things work. He could join the Russian military for a year, gain real-world experience by working in a hospital and receive Russian citizenship. He was led to believe he would then be entitled to some kind of scholarship to finance the remainder of his studies. There was no talk of potentially fighting in the war . Looking back, Peter believes that’s where it all went wrong. “My life changed from how it was before to how it is now,” he said of the moment he signed a one-year military contract. Instead of working in a hospital, Peter was told for the first time that he would be sent to Ukraine. He fretted and protested, but it was ultimately futile. After a few weeks of training, Peter was sent to Donetsk, the Russia-occupied Ukrainian region that has been the epicenter of fighting during the full-scale invasion. “I said, ‘No, I don’t want to go’,” Peter told The Moscow Times. “They said, ‘We will put you in jail for five years’.” Peter was tasked with transporting injured people from the front lines to hospitals in the rear. It was incredibly dangerous. By the end of the first week, he said, 80% of his unit had been killed . But there was nothing he could do to get out of his contract. One day in the fall of 2024, he was caught in an attack . A close friend of his was killed, while Peter’s feet were injured so badly by an explosion that he himself needed to be medically evacuated. One photo shared with The Moscow Times depicts his bandaged foot, blood seeping through the wrappings. Another shows an X-ray scan of the same appendage: where bones should be, there is a hole. Though he had eight surgeries in total, he said the injuries are still debilitating. Peter told The Moscow Times that he has trouble being on his feet, severely limiting his ability to work and quality of life. “I can walk, but I can’t run,” he said. Any distance more than about 700 meters (about half a mile) causes unbearable pain. He was reassigned to a role akin to being a security guard due to his injuries. Months passed and his feet started to hurt again, so he went back to the hospital . But his superiors continued pushing for him to return to the front lines . For Russia, Peter was manpower, and they were going to squeeze every ounce of labor they could from him. By the time he was due to be sent back to the front for a third time, Peter’s 12-month contract had long since expired. When he asked to leave, he said one of his commanders demanded about 400,000 rubles ($5,000). With the help of AI, Peter found Idite Lesom (Get Lost), an NGO that helps Russian servicemembers escape the military. They advised him on what to do next. Under the guise of going to a doctor’s appointment, he slipped away from his unit and made the long trip to Moscow, where he took a rideshare service to Belarus with a plane ticket in hand. The key to escaping, he said, was confidence. “If you’re afraid, they will understand, they will check [your documents],” he said. “But I stayed strong and managed everything.” For servicemembers who desert the Russian military — the number of which may be as high as 50,000, the United Nations estimated last year — the road to a stable life is anything but straightforward. That’s especially true for foreigners, who often face legal obstacles to returning home. “They can’t simply go to the embassy of their country, or to the consulate of their country,” said Idite Lesom spokesperson Ivan Chuviliayev. Because these people are often considered criminals under laws prohibiting foreign mercenary work, “they cannot say that, ‘Well, I was forced to sign a contract and now I want to go home’,” he said. Nevertheless, this is a situation that more people may be finding themselves in as Russia’s war nears its five-year mark and reports point to widespread recruitment efforts directed at African, Latin American and Asian countries. Chuviliayev said his organization has received between 30-40 applications for assistance from non-Russians. However, the rate appears to be increasing. A quarter of those requests came in the month of August alone. For people like Peter, leaving Russia is only half the battle in trying to come to terms with the consequences of military service. Now living outside Russia after deserting just over two months ago, his situation is bleak. Having received Russian citizenship during the course of his service, he is trying to get a new Russian passport while working in retail to make ends meet. He said that he feels trapped, believing simultaneously that he can’t seek help from his home country because of potential legal issues and that the Russian passport he is expecting wouldn’t be helpful in claiming asylum elsewhere, if it arrives at all. “I’m going to try to get a foreign passport so I can leave here and go somewhere in Europe, so I can live peacefully there,” he said. What’s more, he will probably need more operations on his feet — operations that he can’t afford right now. Pakistan has previously denied that its soldiers have taken part in the conflict on the side of Russia. In August 2025, its Foreign Ministry called Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s claims of such activity “unfounded.” The ministry did not respond to The Moscow Time’s request for comment for this story. When asked about his future plans, Peter said he was focused first and foremost on finding a country where he can live comfortably and safely. After that, he might have time to think about returning to his studies and his dreams of being a doctor. To others who might find themselves in a similar position as him, he offered a warning. “If someone in the future wants to go for a [military] contract, I will say please don’t do that,” he said. “They’ll tell you one thing, and when you [sign] the contract they’ll send you to another place.” We are facing unprecedented challenges. https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/0.body_zh: 彼得是一名来自巴基斯坦的24岁男子，2020年前往俄罗斯学习医学。四年后，他却躺在医院的病床上，双脚缠着绷带；这是他在乌克兰前线遭遇爆炸袭击的结果。他最近在另一个国家接受《莫斯科时报》采访时，讲述了自己为俄罗斯军队作战的经历，并因安全原因要求使用化名。他说：“当我签下合同时，我不知道会发生这种事。为了任何报酬、任何护照，我都不会签这份合同。”像其他数以万计的外国人一样，彼得来到俄罗斯，希望过上更好的生活。相反，他说，自己在被骗参军、协助莫斯科对乌克兰发动残酷侵略战争之后，只找到了悲惨的处境。随着全面战争持续近五年，俄罗斯军队越来越依赖外国新兵。然而，冲突拖得越久，这些外国人就越像俄罗斯本国士兵一样逃离部队，这是一个绝望且往往充满恐惧的决定。所有逃兵面临的风险都很高。一旦被抓获，他们可能要在俄罗斯监狱服刑最长10年。对外国新兵而言，逃兵问题还带来独特的挑战，因为其人数可能高达27,000人。许多人面临本国的法律追诉，而不愿提供帮助的国际体系也令他们处境不确定。彼得的经历与那些来到俄罗斯并参军的人有相似之处：国内选择有限，一个全球主要大国承诺提供不受限制的发展机会，一名居心叵测的招募者，一次战场负伤，以及一次绝望的逃亡。在接受《莫斯科时报》两次采访时，彼得讲述了一段将自己的生活分为前后两段的经历，彻底打乱了他对未来的一切规划。由于安全原因，他要求隐去故事中的部分细节，但提供了文件支持自己的说法，包括军事合同副本、医疗记录以及他服役期间的照片。彼得来自巴基斯坦一座小城，一直知道自己想成为一名医生。这是家族传承的职业。然而，等到开始大学学习时，国内的教育费用太高昂。他在国外发现了一个很有希望的机会：俄罗斯南部大城市克拉斯诺达尔的一所大学。该市位于被吞并的克里米亚以西约200公里（124英里）处，他可以在那里以负担得起的费用取得医学学位。他于2020年抵达俄罗斯。彼得很喜欢在俄罗斯的生活。在结交朋友和学习语言的同时，他设想未来可以凭自己的学位在俄罗斯或其他地方获得多种选择。但当家人告诉他已经无法继续提供经济支持时，他的学业也陷入不确定之中。就在那时，一位同样在克拉斯诺达尔学医的朋友告诉他，有一种办法可以让事情步入正轨。他可以参军一年，通过在医院工作获得实际经验，并取得俄罗斯公民身份。他被告知，之后自己将获得某种奖学金，用于支付剩余的学业费用。没有人提及他可能需要参战。彼得现在回望过去，认为一切错误都是从那时开始的。他说，在签下一年期军事合同的那一刻，“我的人生从原来的样子变成了现在的样子”。他没有被安排到医院工作，而是在第一次被告知将被派往乌克兰时，才知道真实情况。他焦虑不安，也提出抗议，但最终无济于事。训练数周后，彼得被派往顿涅茨克——这是俄罗斯占领的乌克兰地区，也是全面入侵期间战斗的中心。Peter对《莫斯科时报》说：“我说：‘不，我不想去。’他们说：‘我们会把你关进监狱五年。’”他的任务是把受伤人员从前线运送到后方医院。这项工作极其危险。他说，第一周结束时，他所在部队80%的士兵已经阵亡。但他无法摆脱合同。2024年秋天的一天，他在一次袭击中被困。一名密友丧生，而彼得的双脚被爆炸严重炸伤，以至于他本人需要接受医疗后送。一张提供给《莫斯科时报》的照片显示，他缠着绷带的脚上有鲜血渗出。另一张照片展示的是同一肢体的X光扫描：骨骼本应所在的位置，只剩一个空洞。尽管他总共接受了8次手术，他说伤势仍令他难以行动。彼得告诉《莫斯科时报》，自己很难长时间站立，严重影响工作能力和生活质量。他说：“我能走，但不能跑。”任何超过约700米（约半英里）的距离都会引发难以忍受的疼痛。由于受伤，他被重新分配到类似保安的岗位。几个月过去后，他的双脚又开始疼痛，于是他回到医院。但上级仍不断催促他返回前线。对俄罗斯而言，彼得就是人力，他们要榨干他身上的每一分劳动力。等到他第三次被派往前线时，12个月的合同早已到期。他提出离开时，据称一名指挥官索要约400,000卢布（$5,000）。在人工智能的帮助下，彼得找到了非政府组织Idite Lesom（意为“滚开”），该组织帮助俄罗斯军人逃离军队，并就下一步该怎么做向他提供建议。他借口去看医生，悄悄离开部队，长途赶往莫斯科，在那里叫了一辆网约车前往白俄罗斯，手里还握着飞机票。他说，逃亡成功的关键是保持信心。“如果你害怕，他们会看出来的，他们会检查[你的文件]，”他说，“但我保持坚强，把一切都安排好了。”对于逃离俄罗斯军队的军人而言，通往稳定生活的道路绝不平坦。联合国去年估计，这类军人可能多达50,000人。对外国人来说尤其如此，他们经常面临回国的法律障碍。Idite Lesom发言人Ivan Chuviliayev说：“他们不能直接去本国大使馆或领事馆。”由于这些人在禁止外国雇佣兵活动的法律下往往被视为罪犯，“他们不能说：‘好吧，我是在被迫的情况下签了合同，现在我想回家。’”尽管如此，随着俄罗斯的战争接近五周年，且有报道显示俄罗斯正针对非洲、拉丁美洲和亚洲国家广泛招募兵员，越来越多的人可能发现自己正身处这种境地。Chuviliayev说，他的组织已经收到30至40份来自非俄罗斯人的援助申请，但这一比例似乎正在上升。仅在8月一个月内，就有四分之一的请求涌入。对彼得这样的人而言，离开俄罗斯只是试图应对参军后果的一半问题。他两个多月前逃兵，如今生活在俄罗斯境外，处境一片黯淡。服役期间，他取得了俄罗斯公民身份，目前一边从事零售工作维持生计，一边试图申领一本新的俄罗斯护照。他说，自己感到受困：一方面，他因潜在的法律问题无法向祖国寻求帮助；另一方面，他正在等待的俄罗斯护照即便拿到，也未必有助于他在其他地方申请庇护。他说：“我会设法拿到一本外国护照，这样我就能离开这里，去欧洲某个地方，在那里平静地生活。”更重要的是，他的双脚可能还需要接受更多手术，而他现在根本负担不起。巴基斯坦此前曾否认本国士兵曾站在俄罗斯一方参与冲突。2025年8月，巴基斯坦外交部称乌克兰总统Volodymyr Zelensky关于相关活动的说法“毫无根据”。外交部没有回应《莫斯科时报》就这篇报道提出的置评请求。当被问及未来计划时，彼得说，首先也是 foremost，他专注于寻找一个能够舒适、安全生活的国家。之后，他才可能有时间考虑重返学业，实现成为一名医生的梦想。对于其他可能发现自己处境与他相似的人，他提出警告。他说：“如果今后有人想签[军事]合同，我要说，请不要这么做。他们会先告诉你一件事，等你[签下]合同后，又把你派到另一个地方。我们正面临前所未有的挑战。俄罗斯总检察长办公室已将《莫斯科时报》列为“ undesirable（不受欢迎）”组织，将我们的工作定性为犯罪，使我们的员工面临被起诉的风险。此前，我们还曾被不公地贴上“外国代理人”标签。这些行动是企图压制俄罗斯独立新闻报道的直接手段。当局声称我们的工作“抹黑俄罗斯领导层的决定”。我们的看法不同：我们致力于提供准确、不偏不倚的俄罗斯报道。我们，《莫斯科时报》的记者，拒绝被噤声。但要继续我们的工作，我们需要你的帮助。无论金额多小的支持，都能带来巨大改变。如果条件允许，请从每月$ 2开始支持我们。设置起来很快，每一笔捐款都能产生显著影响。支持《莫斯科时报》，就是在面对压迫时捍卫开放、独立新闻业。感谢你与我们站在一起。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/when-applaus.title: When applause replaces discernment

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/bett.summary_zh: 第一层 前人道事务与减少贫困部长贝塔·埃杜博士表示，她为总统博拉·蒂努布设定了在2027年大选中从十字河流州获得150万张选票的目标。她说，由第一夫人奥卢雷米·蒂努布发起组织的这项计划旨在改善女性的经济生计，并加强基层动员。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/bett.body: Layer 1 Former Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Betta Edu, has set a target of 1.5 million votes from Cross River for President Bola Tinubu, come 2027 general elections. Edu, Co-Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mobilisation Directorate, made the declaration on Sunday in Calabar, during an empowerment programme that benefited about 500 market women, petty traders and artisans. She said the initiative organised at the instance of the First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, was designed to improve women’s economic livelihood, and strengthen grassroots mobilisation. She said the beneficiaries received N50,000 each, alongside business and household equipment, including deep freezers, blenders, and toasters. According to her, the intervention targets petty traders whose businesses are constrained by inadequate capital. “Some of them are selling trays that have just N5,000 worth of things on them, while some of them have trays with just N10,000 worth of items on them. “So we are giving these sets of petty traders N50,000 each so that they can expand that their business, build on it, so things can get better for them and their children,” she said. Edu urged residents of the state to support Tinubu, Gov. Bassey Otu and other APC candidates as the party was banking on grassroots women’s mobilisation to strengthen its electoral fortunes in the state. She expressed confidence that the state would deliver more than 1.5 million votes for the ruling party, adding that the directorate was establishing support structures for women across the country. She disclosed that the empowerment programme would be extended to other parts of Cross River, with Abi Local Government Area scheduled to benefit in November or December, while the northern senatorial district would be reached in January. The former minister also highlighted some Federal Government interventions, including the student loan scheme and free maternal healthcare, as measures aimed at improving the welfare of Nigerians. As part of the mobilisation activities, she led members of the directorate on a visit to the General Hospital, Calabar, where they interacted with patients, pregnant women and children receiving treatment and offered financial and emotional support. She said the hospital outreach was undertaken at the instance of the First Lady ahead of the APC rally scheduled to hold in Calabar on Monday. Edu also cited subsidised dialysis services and free maternal healthcare as interventions aimed at improving healthcare access and reducing maternal mortality. One of the beneficiaries, Esther Bassey, a widow from Odukpani Local Government Area, expressed appreciation for the support, saying previous empowerment programmes had helped her cater for her three children. Bassey pledged her support for the APC in 2027, saying she and her family would vote for the party Comments expressed here do not reflect the opinions of Vanguard newspapers or any employee thereof
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/bett.title_zh: 贝塔·埃杜争取克诺河州500名女性支持，为蒂努布设定150万张选票目标
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/bett.body_zh: 第一层：前人道事务与减贫部长贝塔·埃杜博士表示，在2027年大选前，她已为总统博拉·蒂努布设定目标，希望从十字河流州争取150万张选票。埃杜是全进步大会党（APC）妇女动员委员会联席主席。星期日，她在卡拉巴尔举行的一项赋权活动上宣布了这一目标。该活动惠及约500名市场妇女、小商贩和手工艺人。她说，这项由第一夫人奥卢雷米·蒂努布发起组织的举措旨在改善妇女的经济生计，并加强基层动员。她说，每名受益者获得了50,000奈拉，以及商用和家用设备，包括深冷冻柜、搅拌机和烤面包机。据她介绍，这项援助面向因资本不足而经营受限的小商贩。“有些人出售的托盘上只有价值5,000奈拉的商品，而另一些人的托盘上也只有价值10,000奈拉的商品。因此，我们向这些小商贩每人提供50,000奈拉，让她们能够扩大经营、继续发展，从而改善自己和孩子的处境。”埃杜呼吁该州居民支持蒂努布、州长巴塞·奥图以及APC的其他候选人，因为该党指望通过动员基层妇女来增强自身在该州的选举优势。她相信，该州将为执政党投出超过150万张选票，并补充说，该委员会正在全国范围内为妇女建立支持网络。她透露，这项赋权活动将延伸至十字河流州其他地区。阿比地方政府辖区计划于11月或12月受益，而北部参议员选区将在1月得到覆盖。这名前部长还介绍了联邦政府的若干干预措施，包括学生贷款计划和免费孕产妇医疗保健，旨在改善尼日利亚国民的福祉。作为动员活动的一部分，她带领委员会成员探访卡拉巴尔综合医院，与正在接受治疗的患者、孕妇和儿童交流，并提供经济及情感支持。她说，此次医院外展活动是在第一夫人推动下开展的，先于定于星期一在卡拉巴尔举行的APC集会。埃杜还提到补贴透析服务和免费孕产妇医疗保健，认为这些措施旨在改善医疗服务可及性并降低孕产妇死亡率。受益者之一、来自奥杜帕尼地方政府辖区的寡妇埃丝特·巴塞对这项支持表示感谢，并表示此前的赋权计划帮助她养育三个孩子。巴塞承诺在2027年支持APC，称她和家人将投票给该党。此处发表的评论不代表《Vanguard》报及其任何员工的观点

https://www.myjoyonline.com/gis-investig.title: GIS investigates explosion that killed officer during Hamile border patrol
https://www.myjoyonline.com/gis-investig.summary: The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) is investigating an explosion during a border patrol operation in the Hamile Sector of the Upper West Region that killed one of its officers and a tricycle rider. The incident occurred in the early hours of Tuesday, November 3, 2026, along an unapproved route in the border area, according to a statement issued by the Service. The GIS said a team of four officers on patrol responded to an unusual sound and intercepted a man transporting a load on a tricycle.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/gis-investig.summary_zh: 加纳移民局（GIS）正在调查一起爆炸事件。事件发生在上西部大区哈米勒区一次边境巡逻行动期间，造成一名移民局官员和一名三轮车驾驶者死亡。该局发表的声明称，事件发生于2026年11月3日凌晨，地点是边境地区一条未经批准的通道。GIS表示，一支由4名官员组成的巡逻队听到异常声响后作出响应，并拦截了一名用三轮车运送货物的人。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/gis-investig.body: The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) is investigating an explosion during a border patrol operation in the Hamile Sector of the Upper West Region that killed one of its officers and a tricycle rider. The incident occurred in the early hours of Tuesday, November 3, 2026, along an unapproved route in the border area, according to a statement issued by the Service. The GIS said a team of four officers on patrol responded to an unusual sound and intercepted a man transporting a load on a tricycle. The rider reportedly attempted to flee as the officers approached to inspect the contents of the load. “In the process of trying to stop him, the load exploded, resulting in the death of the tricycle rider and injuries to two officers,” the statement said

https://www.myjoyonline.com/gis-investig.body_zh: 加纳移民局（GIS）正在调查一起爆炸事件。事件发生在上西部大区哈米勒区边境巡逻行动期间，造成该局一名官员和一名三轮车骑手死亡。该局发表声明称，事件发生于2026年11月3日星期二凌晨，地点是边境地区一条未经批准的通道。GIS表示，一支由4名官员组成的巡逻队听到异常声响后作出响应，并拦截了一名用三轮车运送货物的人。据报道，当官员走近检查货物时，骑手试图逃离。声明称：“在试图制止他的过程中，货物发生爆炸，导致三轮车骑手死亡，另有2名官员受伤。”

https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.title: Germany’s Merz warns Europe needs seat at the table as Trump renews Ukraine talks
https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.summary: BERLIN — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that Europe must help shape any Ukraine peace agreement as U.S. President Donald Trump renews his push to negotiate a deal with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.
https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.summary_zh: 柏林——美国总统唐纳德·特朗普再次推动与其俄罗斯 counterpart弗拉基米尔·普京协商达成协议之际，德国总理弗里德里希·默茨警告，欧洲必须参与塑造任何乌克兰和平协议。
https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.body: BERLIN — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that Europe must help shape any Ukraine peace agreement as U.S. President Donald Trump renews his push to negotiate a deal with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin. “Europe must and wants to play a role in this process,” said Merz alongside Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Berlin Tuesday. “Key elements of a peaceful solution — whether regarding sanctions or the security architecture — can only be resolved with us Europeans. And everyone involved knows that very well.” “The U.S. and Russia — with all due respect to the U.S. — cannot decide whether Ukraine will become a member state of the European Union,” Zelenskyy said. “For that we need the support of other countries, and all of those countries are in Europe.” Merz’s meeting with Zelenskyy in Berlin comes as the Trump administration renews efforts to reach a negotiated end to the full-scale war in Ukraine and before U.S.-brokered talks between Ukraine and Russia are set to resume in Abu Dhabi next week . The meeting in Berlin also comes a day before talks hosted by the European Commission with representatives from the U.S., Ukraine and key European allies on Ukraine’s post-war reconstruction and economic future. Merz also sharply criticized the U.S. decision to invite Russian President Vladimir Putin to December’s G20 summit in Miami, saying the move is shutting Ukraine out of talks about its own fate. “If President Trump were to decide to invite the Russian president, then Ukraine must be the first topic of discussion,” Merz said. “And if Ukraine is discussed, then the president of Ukraine must be seated at the table. In any case, from my perspective, it is completely unacceptable for third countries to discuss Ukraine’s fate without involving Ukraine itself.” European leaders, including Merz, have long feared the U.S. may pursue a Ukraine peace deal on terms that sideline Europe and disadvantage Ukraine
https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.title_zh: 特朗普重启乌克兰谈判之际，德国总理默茨警告欧洲需要参与决策
https://www.politico.eu/article/germany-.body_zh: 柏林——美国总统唐纳德·特朗普再次推动与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京就协议进行谈判之际，德国总理弗里德里希·默茨警告，欧洲必须参与塑造任何乌克兰和平协议。周二，默茨在柏林与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基一同发表讲话时表示：“欧洲必须，也希望在这一进程中发挥重要作用。和平解决方案的关键要素——无论是制裁还是安全架构——只有在我们欧洲人的参与下才能解决。所有相关方都非常清楚这一点。”泽连斯基说：“美国和俄罗斯——充分尊重美国——不能决定乌克兰是否会成为欧盟成员国。为此，我们需要其他国家的支持，而所有这些国家都在欧洲。”此前，特朗普政府正加紧努力，争取通过谈判结束乌克兰全面战争；由美国斡旋的乌克兰与俄罗斯会谈定于下周在阿布扎比恢复。默茨在柏林与泽连斯基会晤之际，欧洲委员会也将在次日主持会谈，邀请美国、乌克兰以及欧洲主要盟友的代表，讨论乌克兰的战后重建与经济未来。默茨还严厉批评美国决定邀请俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京出席12月在迈阿密举行的二十国集团峰会，称此举将乌克兰排除在有关自身命运的讨论之外。默茨说：“如果特朗普总统决定邀请俄罗斯总统，那么乌克兰必须成为讨论的首要议题。而且，如果要讨论乌克兰，乌克兰总统就必须坐在谈判桌旁。无论如何，在我看来，第三方国家不邀请乌克兰参与，就讨论乌克兰的命运，是完全不可接受的。”包括默茨在内的欧洲领导人长期以来一直担心，美国可能会推动一项将欧洲边缘化并使乌克兰处于不利地位的乌克兰和平协议……

https://leadership.ng/asuu-backs-tsu-str.title: ASUU Backs TSU Strike, Urges Kefas To Implement 2025 Agreement
https://leadership.ng/asuu-backs-tsu-str.summary: The ASUU Yola Zone Coordinator, Dani Mamman, made the call on Tuesday during a solidarity visit to the university in Jalingo, where he accused the Taraba State Government of failing to honour its agreement with academic staff.
https://leadership.ng/asuu-backs-tsu-str.summary_zh: 尼日利亚教师工会（ASUU）Yola（地区）协调员Dani Mamman于周二提出这一要求。他当时到Jalingo的大学进行声援访问，指责Taraba（州）政府未能履行与教职员工达成的协议。
https://leadership.ng/asuu-backs-tsu-str.body: The union said TSU was the only university in the North yet to implement the agreed remuneration framework, despite the conclusion of a government-constituted verification exercise. The ASUU Yola Zone Coordinator, Dani Mamman, made the call on Tuesday during a solidarity visit to the university in Jalingo, where he accused the Taraba State Government of failing to honour its agreement with academic staff. Mamman described the delay as a breach of an established agreement and a disregard for the welfare and legitimate entitlements of lecturers, insisting that the grievances of the TSU branch were legitimate and required urgent government intervention. He expressed concern that while other state governments across the North-East had implemented the 2025 agreement, Taraba State was yet to do so, despite the completion of a verification exercise initiated by the state government. According to him, a fact-finding team constituted by the government had established that the universities visited had fully implemented the agreement. He said the report was reportedly presented to the union on September 24, 2026, following a verification exercise that commenced in August. Mamman, however, expressed disappointment that the government was still undertaking salary computations despite the conclusion of the exercise, describing the development as an unnecessary administrative delay. He also faulted the reported consideration of three implementation options of 95 per cent, 98 per cent and 100 per cent, arguing that the verification and financial assessment processes had already been concluded. The ASUU zonal coordinator insisted that the remuneration framework should be implemented in accordance with the payment template contained in the December 23, 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement, which was circulated by the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission on December 30, 2025. He explained that the agreement covered several remuneration components, including Basic CONUASS, Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance, Professorial Allowance, Earned Academic Allowances and responsibility allowances for designated academic and administrative positions. Mamman warned that continued delays could undermine staff retention, institutional competitiveness and the university’s ability to attract qualified academic personnel, with adverse implications for academic standards and institutional stability. He consequently demanded immediate and full implementation of the agreement without further consultations, committees or verification exercises. The union also demanded payment of all accumulated arrears in line with the financial computation submitted by the tripartite committee, strict adherence to the agreed payment template and meaningful engagement with the TSU branch to resolve the ongoing industrial dispute. Mamman said academic staff had demonstrated considerable patience through sustained engagements and constructive dialogue before resorting to industrial action, reaffirming the zonal leadership’s solidarity with the striking lecturers. He maintained that industrial harmony was a collective responsibility and warned that the patience of academic staff should not be taken for granted. The ASUU leader appealed to stakeholders, members of the university community and the general public to prevail on the state government to honour the agreement, clear outstanding entitlements and bring the dispute to an amicable conclusion. The zonal leadership further alleged that TSU remained one of the few universities, if not the only institution among the 19 northern states, yet to implement the agreed remuneration framework. https://leadership.ng/asuu-backs-tsu-str.title_zh: ASUU支持TSU罢工，敦促Kefas落实2025年协议
https://leadership.ng/asuu-backs-tsu-str.body_zh: 工会表示，尽管政府组建的核查工作已经结束，TSU仍是北方唯一尚未落实双方商定薪酬框架的大学。ASUU约拉地区协调员Dani Mamman于周二前往贾林戈对这所大学进行声援访问时提出这一要求，并指责塔拉巴州政府未履行其与学术人员达成的协议。Mamman称，此举拖延既违反既定协议，也无视讲师的福利和合法权益；他坚持认为，TSU分会提出的诉求合理，需要政府立即干预。他表示担忧，东北部其他州政府均已落实2025年协议，但塔拉巴州尽管完成了州政府启动的核查工作，却仍未予执行。据他称，由政府组建的事实调查小组已经确认，受访大学均已全面落实协议。他说，该报告据称于2026年9月24日提交给工会，此前启动的核查工作于8月开始。然而，Mamman对核查结束后政府仍在计算工资感到失望，称这是没有必要的管理拖延。他还批评了据报正在考虑的95%、98%和100%三种落实方案，认为核查和财务评估程序均已结束。ASUU地区协调员坚持认为，薪酬框架应根据2025年12月23日联邦政府与ASUU协议所载的付款模板执行，该模板由National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission于2025年12月30日分发。他解释称，协议涵盖多个薪酬组成部分，包括基本CONUASS、综合学术工具津贴、教授津贴、 Earned Academic Allowances以及指定学术和行政岗位的职责津贴。Mamman警告称，持续拖延可能削弱教职员工的留任率、机构的竞争力以及大学吸引合格学术人才的能力，进而对学术标准和机构稳定造成不利影响。因此，他要求立即全面落实协议，不再进行任何磋商、设立委员会或开展核查。工会还要求，根据三方委员会提交的财务核算结果，支付所有积欠款项；严格遵守商定的付款模板；并与TSU分会展开实质性沟通，以解决持续存在的行业争议。Mamman说，在采取行业行动之前，学术人员通过持续交涉和建设性对话展现了极大的耐心；他再次确认地区领导层声援罢课讲师。他强调，行业和谐是集体责任，并警告称，不应把学术人员的耐心视为理所当然。ASUU负责人呼吁利益相关方、大学社区成员和公众向州政府施压，促使其履行协议、清偿拖欠待遇，并以友好方式结束争议。地区领导层进一步指控称，在北方19个州中，TSU仍是少数尚未落实商定薪酬框架的大学之一，甚至可能是唯一一所这样的院校。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、突发新闻和独家角度将直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时获取全天候更新 →

https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/0.body: U.S. first lady Melania Trump will host representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House this week to deliver remarks on a recently concluded ceasefire and humanitarian mission in the occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the White House announced Tuesday. The six-day ceasefire, which ended Sunday, had allowed emergency aid to reach Oleshky and any civilians to leave if they wanted, either to Ukrainian-controlled territory or Russia. “This achievement marks an unprecedented diplomatic initiative by an American First Lady,” the White House said in a statement, adding that Melania Trump will deliver an address on the Oleshky ceasefire at 11 a.m. Eastern Time on Thursday. It did not name the Russian and Ukrainian representatives invited to appear during the address. A Ukrainian official told The Kyiv Independent that Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova and her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets will attend the White House event. Lantratova is currently under U.S. sanctions and will need a sanctions waiver from the State Department to enter the country. The announcement follows a report in the French newspaper Le Monde that claimed the humanitarian operation in Oleshky was negotiated over the course of four months by Russia’s GRU and Ukraine’s HUR military intelligence agencies. Sources cited by the newspaper suggested that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to credit the first lady for the ceasefire as a way to placate U.S. President Donald Trump as he seeks a diplomatic breakthrough in peace negotiations. Russia and the U.S. confirmed this week that trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine will resume in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10 and 11 after having stalled in February due to the conflict in the Middle East.
